candidate.claim: Critical-line sign separation becomes a certified finite RH result only when conservative numerical errors, overlap checks, and zero-count consistency are combined.
candidate.proposed_limit: The source delegates part of the mathematical certification theorem and full error derivation to earlier papers.
candidate.title: Finite RH certification is a chain of sign evaluation, error bounds, and global counting

parents.context_note: The finite conclusion includes simplicity and critical-line location only within the stated rectangle.
parents.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; large indices suffer spacing OCR but remain identifiable.
parents.selection_reason: Combines an extension beyond the target Gram point, a cited counting theorem, exact reruns where earlier sign shifts affected counts, and spot checks against previous intervals.
parents.title: Extend, overlap, and independently rerun zero-separation intervals before certifying RH

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: the computation extends beyond the target Gram point through five Rosser-valid blocks, then invokes a cited counting theorem to certify that the first 1,500,000,001 zeros are simple and on the critical line in the stated rectangle. A range whose earlier argument shifts made Gram-block and interval counts approximate was rerun without shifts. Additional checks used the vectorized program on another machine and compared selected earlier ranges. Interpretation: finite certification combines endpoint closure with targeted reruns of known bookkeeping vulnerabilities and cross-machine or prior-range overlap. Boundary: these are checks of related program versions and hardware, not demonstrated independently developed implementations, and the conclusion is finite-height only.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts the certification design by separating completeness closure, correction of approximate counts, and overlapping reproducibility checks without inflating their independence.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after revision: it preserves the finite theorem and exact rerun rationale while replacing the critic-flagged independent-implementation overstatement with the actual checks.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The introduction states the extension, the five block lengths, the cited theorem, the exact reason for rerunning the shifted interval, and the selected agreement checks with their machine contexts.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No new speculation; large OCR-spaced indices are used only where the prose makes their identity clear.

parents.context_note: Detailed derivation is omitted by the paper and referred to earlier work; this unit captures only the checked error interface stated here.
parents.representation_dependency: Formula OCR is degraded, but prose and numerical bounds recover the comparison; scan-check exact exponents before reuse.
parents.selection_reason: Separates interpolation error from truncated Riemann-Siegel error, incorporates machine precision, and uses fixed bounds substantially larger than the derived upper bounds.
parents.title: Method-specific dominant errors yield conservative sign certification for Z at Gram points

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: the authors extend a prior rigorous error analysis to the larger height range and account for the CYBER 205's truncated 47- and 94-bit arithmetic. Interpolation dominates the error of method A, while truncation of the two-term Riemann-Siegel expansion dominates method B; other hardware terms are smaller. The fixed bounds actually used are deliberately larger than the derived safe bounds, and method B determines every needed Gram-point sign. Interpretation: an approximation plus an absolute-error envelope is the interface from floating-point output to a certified exact sign. Boundary: the detailed derivation is referred to earlier work, and the stated bounds apply to these methods, machines, and range.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates analytic truncation, interpolation, and arithmetic errors, then explains why a margin converts their combined envelope into a sign certificate.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted: the computational proof interface is concrete and source-grounded, with omitted derivation and implementation scope retained.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Section 2 names the bit widths, dominant sources, derived safe bounds, more conservative operational bounds, and the absence of an unresolved method-B sign.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No new speculation; OCR-damaged exponents are not reproduced exactly.

parents.context_note: The hypothetical harder pattern had not been observed and its first occurrence was unknown.
parents.representation_dependency: Counts and patterns are table-heavy with OCR risk; the checking logic and proposed program change are prose-clear.
parents.selection_reason: Gives a counting consistency relation, documents monotone frequency changes, classifies 3,055 exceptions, and identifies the first zero-pattern that a simple adjacent-block recovery would miss.
parents.title: Zero-count identities and adjacent-block searches audit exceptions to Rosser's rule

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: a counting identity relating the numbers of Gram intervals with j zeros supplies an internal consistency check. The run classifies 3,055 Rosser exceptions; every observed missing pair lies in the preceding or succeeding block. The source then gives an unobserved 0,0,1,3-type configuration for which searching only the nearest adjacent block would fail. Interpretation: the count identity audits conservation of zeros, while the hypothetical pattern is a counterfactual completeness test for an empirically successful recovery heuristic. Boundary: adjacent-block recovery worked on all observed exceptions but is not logically complete, and the source does not specify a complete replacement algorithm.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Connects an invariant and an adversarial pattern to distinguish correctness checks from search completeness.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted: the unit supports an exact audit mechanism and a concrete failure condition without turning empirical success into a proof of completeness.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The prose following Table 5 states the identity, total exception count, observed missing-pair locations, interactive search procedure, proposed integration, and the simplest pattern that defeats it.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The harder pattern and its first occurrence remain unknown; any broader-search design is inference rather than a source-prescribed algorithm.

candidate.claim: Length-conditioned block frequencies and extreme configurations look structured, but sparse tails and drifting frequencies make the explanatory law an open question.
candidate.proposed_limit: The reported run predates the later random-matrix framework and supplies finite empirical evidence only.
candidate.title: Rare Gram phenomena need a probabilistic model, not extrapolation from tables

parents.context_note: Tables are finite empirical evidence and the authors explicitly say length-seven data are insufficient.
parents.representation_dependency: Table extraction is noisy; use the original scan for exact counts, while qualitative trends are stated in prose.
parents.selection_reason: Reports exact counts, changing block-length frequencies, outer-interval concentration of missing zeros, and tentative convergence for shorter blocks while withholding claims where samples are sparse.
parents.title: Gram-block types drift toward length-dependent symmetric-looking distributions

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: exact finite counts over 1.5 billion Gram intervals show a slowly decreasing fraction of length-one blocks, increasing longer blocks, and, for several fixed lengths, type frequencies that appear to approach length-dependent distributions with missing zeros favoring outer intervals. The authors explicitly withhold a limiting claim for sparsely sampled lengths at least seven. Interpretation: conditioning on block length exposes a pattern hidden by aggregate occupancy, while changes across height reveal finite-range drift rather than a frozen law. Approximate reflection of paired type frequencies is empirical, not a symmetry theorem. Boundary: the tables do not identify or prove convergence to any probability distribution.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Reorganizes the data by conditioning variable and separates stable-looking within-length shape from across-height drift and sampling uncertainty.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted: it preserves finite-evidence status and uses the exact conditioning structure to produce a non-generic conceptual reading.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The prose surrounding Tables 1-3 states the average block length, height trends, outer-interval tendency, tentative limits through the better-sampled lengths, and sample insufficiency for longer blocks.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Limiting distributions and symmetry remain source-marked empirical suggestions; individual OCR-noisy table entries require scan verification.

parents.context_note: These are observed records in the finite run, not asymptotic causal claims.
parents.representation_dependency: Exact table entries and indices require scan verification; captions and surrounding prose preserve the semantic observations.
parents.selection_reason: Connects rare block patterns with local S extrema, gives a normalized closest-zero separation, and shows the largest observed positive and negative Gram-point values occur with unusually wide neighboring zero spans.
parents.title: Rosser exceptions, S extremes, a closest pair, and large Gram-point values probe finite tails

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: the finite run records Rosser-exception types and local extremes of S, a closest observed zero pair with normalized separation about 0.00034, and the largest sampled positive and negative Gram-point Z values. The latter occur between neighboring zeros separated by about 3.85 and 3.65 local Gram intervals. Interpretation: normalizing gaps permits comparison across height, while S, block pattern, gap, and amplitude provide multiple observables of rare local configurations. Their co-occurrence generates hypotheses but does not supply a causal mechanism or asymptotic frequency. Boundary: these are records from one finite computation, not evidence of tail independence or a limiting law.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Places heterogeneous rare-event measurements on comparable local scales and explicitly audits the reach of correlations seen in the finite sample.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted: the interpretation preserves the finite empirical content and adds a disciplined joint-tail reading without overpromotion.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Tables 6-9 and the surrounding prose state the exception records, normalized close-pair value, sampled Z extremes, and neighboring spans.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No asymptotic or causal claim is adopted; exact indices and table cells remain scan-dependent.

parents.context_note: The authors explicitly do not trace downstream numerical consequences of the larger bound.
parents.selection_reason: Summarizes apparent convex type distributions, asks for a probabilistic model, and distinguishes improved finite verification bounds from progress toward a proof of RH.
parents.title: Finite Gram statistics suggest but do not explain an unknown probabilistic law

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: the authors say the observed Gram-block type frequencies for lengths three through six appear to tend to length-dependent discrete convex distributions and ask for a probabilistic model that could explain them. They separately note that results depending on a finite verified-height parameter may improve after the larger computation, but do not trace those consequences. Interpretation: the computation ends by identifying a compression problem: replace many empirical type counts by a testable probability law. That missing model is distinct from enlarging a finite RH verification range. Boundary: no limiting distribution, downstream bound, or global evidence for RH is established here.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates explanatory model-building from finite certification and identifies the exact observable a future theory must reproduce.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted: the open problem is source-explicit, mathematically auditable, and clearly separated from stronger proof claims.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The discussion section explicitly states the apparent convex distributions, asks for a probabilistic model, notes possible parameter-dependent consequences, and says they were not pursued.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The limiting distributions are tentative and the downstream finite consequences are uncomputed.
